proof_audit.v13-c04-economy: Pass. The same commodity/date/location convention, net supply and complete ownership sum give p·z≤0 from budgets, and equality only after exhaustion. Homogeneous profits and owner incomes scale with prices. All direct Cobb–Douglas cases separately exclude zero-price nonattainment and do not falsely invoke global strict coordinate monotonicity.
proof_audit.v13-c04-sperner: Pass. Ordered barycentric-coordinate drops are nonnegative and reconstruct every point. Ties delete precisely the nonshared chain vertices, proving common-face compatibility, including restrictions to old faces. Triangular coordinates establish nondegeneracy; nested-face averages prove geometric mesh decay. Each marked facet has one boundary or two interior incidences; simplex contributions 1/2/0 and the inherited opposite-face labeling complete the dimension induction from d=0.
proof_audit.v13-c04-brouwer: Pass. Every nonfixed simplex vertex has a strictly positive deficit, whose index cannot be a zero coordinate. A compact subsequence of one full-cell vertex and vanishing cell diameter give a common limit for all labels; coordinate sums force equality. Nearest-point attainment, strict midpoint uniqueness and the two variational inequalities prove continuous nonexpansive projection. The explicit containing simplex then extends Brouwer to compact convex sets with empty ambient interior.
proof_audit.v13-c04-kakutani: Pass. Compact range is expressly used to extract an image subsequence in the closed-graph/UHC implication. Finite nets make tent denominators positive; convex range makes their averages eligible for the proved Brouwer theorem. All active sites approach the same limit uniformly. UHC puts selected values near the limiting image, whose compactness and convexity allow nearby averaged image points; closedness gives final membership. No arbitrary continuous selection or circular Nash theorem is presumed.
proof_audit.v13-c04-existence: Pass. Compact generator supports, not the full potentially unbounded disposal argmax, provide representatives and resource bounds. Individual positive endowments ensure positive continuous income and the explicit lower budget approximation. Demand/supply/auction values are nonempty compact convex with proved closed graphs. At a product fixed point auction plus owner accounting first gives z≤0; feasibility puts choices below caps, then strict monotonicity excludes zero prices and permits exhaustion. Positive prices convert Walras equality into exact clearing. Preferred uncapped choices are shrunk to cheaper preferred bundles; weak convex mixtures plus a separate strict coordinate increase contradict capped optimality.
proof_audit.v13-c04-limits: Pass. The theorem is only a sufficient compact-generator class. The Leontief positive-price family has separately qualified weak monotonicity; linear preferences satisfy the theorem yet permit an allocation continuum. Unique scalar fixed points need not attract iteration. Strictly coordinate-increasing quadratic preferences can have nonconvex upper contours and no equilibrium at any positive or boundary price. Mean-feasible lotteries change deterministic feasibility.

additional_witnesses: A nonlinear simplex-interval map has a fully labeled dyadic cell of width 1/256 whose rational midpoint is not fixed; the limit step remains essential.
For F(x)={x²}, sites 0 and 1 with epsilon=2 yield a tent-map fixed point at 1/2, although 1/2 is not in F(1/2). Finite averaging alone is insufficient.
The closed graph F(0)={0}, F(x)={1/x} for x>0 has escaping images and fails UHC at zero; this explicitly shows the need for the compact-range qualification.
